steps.stem: Three weeks after Nurit replaced the yellowish lighting in her bookstore with strong white lighting, she found that her sales had dropped by about a fifth. She attributed the drop to the new lighting, which in her opinion discourages customers from browsing at length among the shelves. Which of the following statements strengthens Nurit's explanation?
choices: Most of the customers of the store are students from the nearby college
In the pharmacy across the street, which has been lit with white light for years, there are always many customers
Ten days before the lighting was replaced, a large bookstore that sells books at a discount opened in the same street
In the weeks after the change, the customers spent on average much less time in the store than before
explanation: Nurit's explanation is that the lighting shortened the customers' browsing, and (4) shows that this is exactly what happened. (1) is irrelevant, (2) is a counterexample, and (3) offers another cause of the drop.

steps.stem: Ziva saw her neighbor, Mr. Adler, leave several wooden chairs painted bright yellow on the sidewalk for the garbage collectors. She concluded that Mr. Adler does not like yellow furniture. Which of the following statements does not weaken Ziva's conclusion?
choices: Every piece of furniture in Mr. Adler's apartment is painted yellow
The chairs Mr. Adler put out had cracked or wobbly legs
Mr. Adler received the yellow chairs as a gift a month before his wedding
Mr. Adler's daughter had recently bought him a new dining set
explanation: When and how he got the chairs says nothing about why he threw them out. (1), (2) and (4) each give a reason other than dislike of yellow.

steps.stem: Dr. Elkin divided twelve volunteers into two teams, one of three and one of nine, and gave each team an hour to find as many as possible of small objects that had been hidden in a garden. Each team searched in a different garden, and the two gardens were of the same size. The team of nine found three times as many objects as the team of three, and Elkin hypothesized that in tasks of this kind, the size of the team affects its success. Which of the following statements strengthens Elkin's hypothesis?
choices: One of the members of the large team had helped to hide the objects before the experiment
The members of the small team had taken part in such searches before, and those of the large team had not
In the garden in which the small team searched, the objects were hidden in more difficult places
The large team searched in the morning, and the small team at noon, when it was very hot
explanation: The larger team won even though experience was on the smaller team's side, which rules out experience as an explanation. (1), (3) and (4) each offer another reason why the large team found more.

steps.stem: Given: The proportion of people with dry skin among those who use a certain skin cream is higher than their proportion in the general population. Hypothesis: Dry skin is a side effect of using the cream. Which of the following findings weakens the hypothesis?
choices: People who use a different cream instead of this one do not suffer from dry skin
Dermatologists recommend this cream only to people who do not have dry skin
The cream is meant to relieve the itching caused by dry skin
One of the common side effects of the cream is a mild rash
explanation: If the cream is used because of dry skin, the dry skin comes first and the cream follows: cause and effect are reversed. (2) supports the hypothesis, and (1) and (4) do not bear on it.

steps.stem: Yigal, who suffers from a burning in his mouth after spicy meals, noticed that on the evenings on which he ate a vanilla pudding after dinner, the burning passed quickly. He concluded that vanilla neutralizes the burning caused by spicy food. Which of the following does not weaken Yigal's conclusion?
choices: Yigal also drinks coffee with vanilla almost every morning
Yigal eats the pudding straight from the refrigerator, and the burning in his mouth passes more quickly when he eats something cold
On the evenings on which Yigal ate the pudding, he usually ate a smaller and less spicy dinner
On most evenings on which Yigal did not eat the pudding, the burning also passed quickly
explanation: His morning coffee says nothing about whether vanilla eases the burning. (2) offers another cause of the relief (the cold), (3) a smaller and milder meal, and (4) shows that the burning passed quickly even without the pudding.

steps.stem: In a certain youth orchestra, a player who is absent from a rehearsal without notice must, at the next rehearsal, help the orchestra's caretaker to arrange the chairs and the music stands. Last month the caretaker was on leave, and the number of absences without notice was much lower than usual. The conductor concluded that the obligation to help the caretaker does not deter the players from being absent, since they enjoy his company. Which of the following facts may weaken the conductor's conclusion?
choices: Two months ago both the number of absences and the number of players who were sent to help the caretaker reached a record
At the beginning of last month it was announced that only players who had not been absent would perform with the orchestra abroad
When the caretaker returned from his leave, the number of absences rose again
Last month the players' school examination period began, and they had less free time than usual
explanation: An announcement made at the same time offers another reason for the drop in absences. (3) supports the conductor, (4) should have raised absences, so the drop despite it also supports the conclusion, and (1) says nothing about last month.

steps.title: Strengthen and weaken: the toolkit
steps.intro: Every choice adds data. Ask which way it pushes the conclusion.

head: Weakens
Strengthens
rows: !Alternative explanation – another reason for the same data
!Negating an alternative explanation – the other reason is ruled out (or works against the result)
Counterexample – the cause without the effect
Supporting evidence – the claimed mechanism shows up in the data
Chicken and egg – cause and effect swapped
Undermining the basis – the data behind the conclusion is shaky
Strengthening the basis – the data becomes even stronger

tips: Gambler test: bet on the conclusion. Does the new fact shake your bet?
'Does not weaken': cross out the 3 that weaken. The answer may be irrelevant, not only strengthening.
Flip test: if the flipped fact weakens, the original strengthens.
Watch whether the data is a number or a percentage.
A clear-cut alternative explanation: mark it and move on.

steps.stem: A developmental psychologist asked seven-year-olds in two schools to copy a drawing of a house. Most of the children in the first school copied it accurately, whereas most of the drawings from the second school were inaccurate. The psychologist concluded that the ability to copy a drawing develops later among the children of the second school. Which of the following does not weaken her conclusion?
choices: Children in the second school are taught that copying another person's work is wrong, and many of them deliberately drew a house of their own design
Most of the houses in the second school's neighborhood look very different from the house in the drawing, and many children drew the kind of house they see every day
The proportion of children with poor eyesight is considerably higher in the first school than in the second
When asked to copy a drawing of a tree, the children of the second school were as accurate as those of the first
explanation: Poorer eyesight in the first school would make its children's success harder, not easier, so it does not explain away the gap. (1) and (2) give other reasons for the inaccurate drawings, and (4) shows that the children of the second school can copy.

steps.stem: Ofer's orchid had not flowered in the four months since he bought it. He then moved it from the living room to the kitchen, where the air is more humid, and two weeks later it flowered. Ofer concluded that orchids of this kind flower only when the air is humid. Which of the following statements can weaken Ofer's conclusion?
choices: Ofer's neighbor keeps an orchid of the same kind in her kitchen, and it too flowered this month
In the wild, orchids of this kind grow high on the branches of trees in tropical forests
Ofer waters the orchid once a week, exactly as the florist advised him
Orchids of this kind usually stop flowering for several months after they are moved to a new home
explanation: If such orchids stop flowering for some months after a move, this one may have flowered simply because enough time had passed. (1) and (2) are consistent with the conclusion, and (3) does not bear on it.

steps.stem: For the past two summers, a music festival has been held in the courtyard of an old caravanserai. Last year the organizers ran an extensive radio campaign, yet attendance did not rise. One of the organizers argued that the courtyard is simply too small to hold more visitors. Which of the following statements can weaken the organizer's argument?
choices: Neither last year nor the year before were all the tickets for any of the festival's evenings sold
Next year the festival is to move to the town's soccer stadium, which can hold three times as many people
Last year tickets were cheaper than the year before, and students were offered an additional discount
In a survey, most people who had heard the radio advertisements could remember the festival's name
explanation: If the tickets never sold out, the size of the courtyard did not limit attendance. (2) is consistent with the argument, (3) makes the result more surprising without weakening the argument, and (4) does not bear on it.

steps.stem: Researchers studied how the location of an exhibition in a museum affects attendance. Over a year, they counted the visitors to each of the museum's exhibitions and found that exhibitions shown in the hall next to the entrance drew more visitors than those shown elsewhere. They concluded that placing an exhibition next to the entrance increases the number of people who visit it. Which of the following weakens the researchers' conclusion?
choices: Most visitors spend less than two hours in the museum, and many leave before they have seen all the halls
Each year the museum assigns the hall next to the entrance to the exhibition it expects to be the most popular
Exhibitions of embroidery attract more visitors than exhibitions of pottery, regardless of the hall in which they are shown
Visitors who come with guided groups see only the halls the guide chooses, rather than those they would choose themselves
explanation: If the exhibition expected to be most popular is placed next to the entrance, its location does not explain its popularity. (1) if anything supports the conclusion, and (3) and (4) do not bear on the link between location and attendance.

steps.stem: Several years ago a municipality installed speed cameras on its main street. Since then, the number of accidents on the street has dropped by 30%. The municipality now plans to install cameras on all the city's streets, claiming that this will reduce the number of accidents throughout the city. The answer to which of the following questions will not help to determine whether the municipality's claim is correct?
choices: How was the money collected from the fines used?
Were other changes made on the main street during those years, such as new traffic lights or wider sidewalks?
Did the number of accidents in the other streets of the city also drop during those years?
Is the main street different from the other streets in the city in the amount of traffic or in the speed at which people drive on it?
explanation: The use of the fine money has nothing to do with whether cameras reduce accidents. (2) and (3) check whether the drop was caused by the cameras, and (4) checks whether the result on the main street can be applied to other streets.

steps.stem: A study found that children who eat breakfast at the same time every day get higher grades than children who eat breakfast at different times. Following the study, a school principal recommended that parents have their children eat breakfast at the same time every day. A psychologist argued that the recommendation was unjustified. Which of the following could be the basis for her argument?
choices: Children who eat breakfast at the same time every day do not eat more, on average, than children who eat it at different times
The grades of the children in the study were below the national average, both among those who eat at the same time and among the others
Children who eat breakfast at the same time also tend to go to bed at a regular hour, and their parents tend to keep a close eye on their schoolwork
Most parents do not follow recommendations of this kind
explanation: If these children also come from orderly homes that follow their schoolwork, their grades may be due to their homes and not to the time of breakfast. (1) rules out one mechanism but not the connection, and (2) and (4) do not bear on the comparison.

steps.stem: This year, many more thefts were reported to the police in a rural district than last year. A local council member concluded that thefts in the district have increased. Which of the following weakens his conclusion?
choices: Last year the police caught most of the people who committed thefts in the district
Most of the thefts reported this year involved small sums of money left in unlocked cars
About forty new families moved to the district this year, most of them from the large cities in the center of the country
Until this year, residents who wished to report a theft had to travel to a police station in the nearest town
explanation: If reporting became much easier this year, the number of reports may have risen although the number of thefts did not. (3) could explain a real rise, and (1) and (2) do not bear on the comparison.

steps.stem: In recent years, many old carob trees in one region have stopped bearing fruit. The regional agronomist attributes this to the decline in rainfall, while a researcher at the Ministry of Agriculture attributes it to a fungus carried by a beetle that reached the region about ten years ago. Which of the following findings weakens the agronomist's explanation without supporting the researcher's?
choices: Trees that were irrigated regularly stopped bearing fruit at the same rate as trees that were not irrigated
Trees that were sprayed against beetles every spring have continued to bear fruit as before
In a neighboring region, where rainfall has not declined, the carob trees continue to bear fruit
The trees bore the least fruit in the years in which the beetle was most widespread
explanation: Regular irrigation makes up for the lack of rain, so if irrigated trees were affected just as much, rainfall is not the cause; this says nothing about the beetle. (2) and (4) support the researcher, and (3) supports the agronomist.

steps.stem: An ophthalmologist noticed that many of the patients who come to him with a certain eye disease are truck drivers. He concluded that driving for many hours increases the risk of the disease. Which of the following strengthens his conclusion?
choices: His clinic is next to the country's largest truck depot, and many drivers come to him simply because it is convenient for them
Among bus drivers, the disease is more common among those who drive long intercity routes than among those who drive in the city
The disease tends to run in families, and many of his patients have relatives who also suffer from it
Many truck drivers suffer from back pain and headaches, which doctors also attribute to long hours at the wheel without a break
explanation: Finding more of the disease among other drivers whose driving is longer supports the conclusion. (1) offers another reason why many truck drivers come to this clinic, (3) points to heredity, and (4) concerns other complaints.

steps.stem: Medieval manuscripts copied in one monastery contain far fewer errors than those copied in a neighboring monastery. One scholar attributes the difference to the better training of the first monastery's copyists; another argues that they simply worked more slowly. Which of the following, if true, would explain the difference without relying on either scholar's explanation?
choices: Most of the first monastery's copyists had learned their craft at the second monastery before moving
The copyists of the first monastery copied fewer pages a day than those of the second, and rested more often
The second monastery was much larger than the first, and many more copyists worked in its scriptorium
In the first monastery, each page was read by a second monk after it had been copied, and he corrected the errors he found
explanation: If each page was checked and corrected afterwards, the difference is explained without better training or slower work. (1) weakens the first explanation but explains nothing, (2) supports the second, and (3) does not explain the difference.

steps.stem: A novelist's second book sold far fewer copies than his first. His publisher believes that this is because the second book was more expensive. Which of the following does not weaken the publisher's explanation?
choices: Shortly after the first novel came out, it was adapted into a television series that was broadcast on the main channel
The second novel is almost twice as long as the first, and many readers complained that it is hard going
The novelist's third book, which was cheaper than the other two, sold more copies than either of them
The first novel was published shortly after the author won a well-known literary prize, which the newspapers covered widely
explanation: The success of the cheaper third book is consistent with the publisher's explanation. (1), (2) and (4) offer other reasons for the difference in sales.

steps.stem: Over the past fifteen years, the rate of a certain skin disease has been higher in one of the country's coastal cities than in its other cities. Researchers assume that the reason is the high humidity in that city. Which of the following does not weaken the researchers' assumption?
choices: The drinking water in the coastal city contains more chlorine than the water in other cities, and chlorine increases the risk of the disease
The disease is most common among young children, and the proportion of young children in the coastal city is lower than in other cities
Until a power station was built near the city three years ago, the humidity in the city was low
In another city the humidity is even higher, but the disease is rare there
explanation: If the city has fewer young children, its higher rate of the disease is even harder to explain by its population, so (2) does not weaken the assumption. (1) offers another cause, (3) shows that the humidity was low during most of the period, and (4) shows high humidity without the disease.

steps.stem: A municipality is planning to build a large parking garage downtown, so that drivers will no longer have to circle the streets in search of a space. Opponents of the plan argue that the garage will actually increase downtown traffic. Which of the following does not support the opponents' argument?
choices: When parking is easy to find, more people drive downtown instead of taking the bus
In other cities, the number of cars entering the city center rose after large garages were built there
At the end of the working day, long lines of cars form at the exits of large garages and block the surrounding streets
A large share of downtown traffic consists of drivers looking for a parking space
explanation: If much of the traffic consists of drivers looking for parking, a garage would reduce it, as the plan claims. (1), (2) and (3) support the opponents.

steps.stem: In an international survey, workers in two neighboring countries were asked to rate their job satisfaction on a scale of 1 to 10. The average rating in the first country was higher than in the second. Professor Weisser argues that this does not show that workers in the first country are more satisfied with their jobs. Which of the following could be the basis for her argument?
choices: In the second country it is considered immodest to express great satisfaction, and people who are very pleased with something usually describe it as merely "reasonable"
Wages in the first country are higher, and people with higher wages tend to be more satisfied with their jobs
The percentage of respondents who chose 6 was the same in both countries
Several hundred questionnaires from the first country were left out by mistake, and the average rating in them was even higher than in those that were counted
explanation: If people in the two countries use the scale differently, the averages do not measure the same thing. (2) supports the gap, (4) would widen it, and (3) is beside the point.

steps.stem: Tamar, who teaches folk dancing, noticed that few of her students are over 50, and assumed that people over 50 are less interested in dancing than younger people. Something a friend told her made her change her mind. Which of the following is most likely to be what her friend told her?
choices: The hall in which Tamar teaches is very hot in the summer, and many of her students stop coming in July and August
A teacher in the neighboring town holds classes especially for people over 50 on the same evenings, and they are always full
When Tamar lowered her fees for people over 50 last year, their number in her classes did not rise at all
Among Tamar's students there are more people in their twenties than in their thirties or forties
explanation: If people over 50 fill classes elsewhere, they are interested in dancing but go elsewhere. (3) supports Tamar's assumption, and (1) and (4) do not bear on the interest of people over 50.

steps.stem: Tea made from the leaves of a certain plant is known to improve concentration. A pharmaceutical company assumed that one of the substances in the leaves was responsible, and produced capsules containing that substance alone. People who took the capsules showed no improvement in concentration, and the company's researchers concluded that the substance is not responsible for the effect. Which of the following would strengthen the researchers' conclusion?
choices: Tea made from leaves from which the substance had been removed improved concentration as much as ordinary tea
Tea made from other plants, which do not contain the substance, does not improve concentration
The people who drank the tea in the original studies had slept less than usual the night before
The capsules also contained a second substance, which prevents the body from absorbing the first when the two are taken together
explanation: If the tea works just as well without the substance, the substance is not what causes the effect. (2) supports the original assumption, (4) explains the capsules' failure and so weakens the conclusion, and (3) does not bear on it.

steps.stem: While researching the history of a small town, a historian read every issue of the local newspaper for 1921 and found no report of a flood that year. She concluded that there was no flood in the town in 1921. Which of the following weakens her conclusion?
choices: The newspaper reported on every event in the town, however minor, including fires in single houses
According to the records of a nearby weather station, very little rain fell in the region in the winter of 1921
There were floods in the town in 1920 and in 1922, and the newspaper reported both of them in detail
In the winter of 1921 the newspaper did not appear for four months, because its printing press had broken down
explanation: If the newspaper did not appear during the rainy months of 1921, a flood could have occurred without being reported. (1), (2) and (3) support the conclusion or do not bear on it.

steps.stem: Until the middle of the twentieth century, the inhabitants of a certain island drank very little coffee, and few cases of a certain heart disease were recorded there. Today coffee is the most popular drink on the island, and the number of recorded cases of the disease has risen sharply. Researchers concluded that drinking coffee increases the risk of the disease. Which of the following weakens the researchers' conclusion?
choices: Life expectancy on the island is still higher than on any of the neighboring islands
Until thirty years ago there was no hospital on the island, and people who complained of chest pain were rarely examined
Islanders who have moved to the mainland, where much coffee is drunk, suffer from the disease as often as other mainlanders
Most of the islanders drink their coffee black, whereas on the mainland it is usually drunk with milk
explanation: If people with heart complaints were rarely examined in the past, many cases went unrecorded, and the rise may reflect diagnosis rather than more illness. (1), (3) and (4) do not show that the rise is not real.

steps.stem: Rina wanted to find out which of eight shades of paint her grandparents would prefer for their living room. One evening she showed them the samples one after another and asked them to give each a score. The lightest shade received the highest score, and Rina concluded that this is the shade her grandparents prefer. Which of the following weakens Rina's conclusion?
choices: The samples were shown in dim light, in which the darker shades looked almost identical
Rina's grandfather has been painting landscapes in oils for many years and is considered an expert on color
Her grandmother's favorite color is light blue, which was not among the eight samples
Her grandparents spend most of their time in the kitchen and the garden and rarely sit in the living room
explanation: In dim light the darker shades could not be judged properly, so the lightest may have won for that reason alone. (2) and (4) do not bear on the test, and (3) concerns a color that was not tested.

steps.stem: A company offered its sales staff an optional course in negotiation. At the end of the year, the sales manager found that those who had taken the course had not sold more than those who had not, and concluded that the course had been useless. Which of the following weakens the manager's conclusion?
choices: The course was taught by a lecturer who had never worked in sales himself
The salespeople who took the course are among the most experienced in the company
At another company, salespeople who took a similar course sold less than their colleagues who did not
Most of those who took the course had joined the company only a few months earlier
explanation: New salespeople would be expected to sell less; if they sold as much as their experienced colleagues, the course may well have helped. (2) strengthens the conclusion, and (1) and (3) do not weaken it.

steps.stem: To find out whether a new fertilizer increases the yield of his tomatoes, a farmer treated half of his field with it and cultivated the other half as usual. At harvest time the treated half yielded more tomatoes, and the farmer concluded that the fertilizer increases the yield. Which of the following does not weaken the farmer's conclusion?
choices: The treated half of the field faces south and gets several more hours of sun each day than the other half
In each of the three previous years, too, this half of the field yielded more tomatoes than the other half
The company that makes the fertilizer does not disclose which of its ingredients is responsible for its effect
During the season, the farmer's family picked tomatoes from the untreated half for their own use, and these were not weighed
explanation: Not knowing which ingredient works does not cast doubt on the fertilizer's effect. (1) and (2) offer other reasons for the difference, and (4) shows that the untreated half yielded more than was counted.

steps.stem: Last month, sales of electric fans at an appliance store in Beersheba rose by 40%. The store's owner attributed the rise to the heat wave that hit the region that month. Which of the following weakens the owner's explanation?
choices: Sales of air conditioners at the store rose that month by an even higher percentage
It was the longest heat wave recorded in the region in twenty years
During that month, the store gave a second fan free to every customer who bought one
During that month, another appliance store on the same street cut the prices of its fans
explanation: A free second fan is another reason for the rise in the number of fans sold. (1) and (2) support the explanation, and (4) would, if anything, have lowered the store's sales.

steps.stem: A statistics lecturer noticed that all the history students in her course hand in their assignments late. She concluded that students who take a course outside their own department do not make an effort to hand in assignments on time. Which of the following statements can strengthen the lecturer's conclusion?
choices: Economics students who take courses in the history department also tend to hand in their assignments late
The history students hand in their assignments late in all their courses, including those in their own department
Several of the statistics students in the course also hand in their assignments late
In the middle of the semester, the history students have to submit long seminar papers in their own department
explanation: Late work from other students taking courses outside their department shows that the pattern is not limited to the history students. (2) and (4) offer other explanations for the history students' lateness, and (3) does not support the conclusion.

steps.stem: A report on road accidents in a small town found that most accidents involving local drivers occurred less than five kilometers from the drivers' homes. A local journalist concluded that drivers are less careful near home than farther away. Which of the following weakens the journalist's conclusion?
choices: The town is smaller than the other towns in the region, and fewer accidents occur there each year
Most of the trips made by the town's drivers are to work, shops and schools within the town itself
In a neighboring town, most accidents involving local drivers occurred far from the drivers' homes
Drivers on a road they know well pay less attention to road signs than drivers on an unfamiliar road
explanation: If most driving is done near home, it is not surprising that most accidents happen there, even if drivers are equally careful everywhere. (4) supports the journalist, and (1) and (3) do not bear on the comparison.

steps.stem: In a study, elementary school teachers arranged the desks in their classrooms in a circle for one week and in rows facing the board for another. When the desks were in a circle, the children took part in class discussions more often. The researchers concluded that children speak more freely when they can see one another's faces. Which of the following does not weaken the researchers' conclusion?
choices: The week in which the desks were in rows was the last week before the exams, when many children were busy studying
When the desks were in rows, the children at the back could hardly hear what the children in front of them said
The chairs used in the circle were new and comfortable, whereas those used in the rows were old and hard
In both weeks the teachers asked the same number of questions and raised the same topics for discussion
explanation: That the teachers asked the same questions in both weeks rules out one other explanation, so it does not weaken the conclusion. (1), (2) and (3) offer other reasons why the children spoke less when the desks were in rows.

steps.stem: This year Ze'ev's pomegranate tree yielded more fruit than the tree in his neighbor Dalia's garden. Ze'ev attributes the difference to the variety he planted, while Dalia attributes it to the fact that his tree gets more sun. Which of the following is inconsistent with both explanations?
choices: The two trees are of the same variety and were bought at the same nursery in the same year
Pomegranate trees that get more sun generally yield more fruit than trees growing in partial shade
Last year, when both trees stood where they stand now, Dalia's tree yielded more fruit than Ze'ev's
Trees of the variety Ze'ev planted generally yield more fruit than trees of other varieties
explanation: Last year the variety and the sun were the same as this year, yet Dalia's tree yielded more, so neither factor accounts for this year's difference. (1) is inconsistent only with Ze'ev's explanation, (2) supports Dalia's, and (4) supports Ze'ev's.

steps.stem: Most of the bridal shops in a certain town are on one street. A young designer who is planning to open a bridal shop was advised not to open it on that street because of the competition. Which of the following weakens this advice?
choices: The long-established shops on the street sometimes copy the designs of new shops and sell them more cheaply within weeks
Brides looking for a gown usually spend a whole day on that street and visit almost every shop on it
Rents on that street are almost twice as high as in the town's other shopping areas
The workshops that sew the gowns for the shops are all in the industrial zone, on the other side of town
explanation: If brides come to that street and visit almost every shop on it, a new shop there will be seen by many buyers despite the competition. (1), (3) and (4) support the advice.
